report.headline: The $2,400 RET claim is rejected because the returned sofa was a disclosed, accepted custom COM order that was final sale.
report.executive_summary: The Card Member correctly identified the disputed $2,400 charge, but the Merchant's refusal was permitted by the accepted Checkout Terms. The order was for one Alder three-seat sofa in Customer's Own Material (COM). Checkout Terms v4, accepted by checkbox before payment, expressly state that COM or made-to-measure pieces are final sale and cannot be returned or refunded. The website's general 30-day policy expressly excludes custom orders and refers to the same clause. The return attempt was refused and no credit was issued, but that conduct was consistent with the applicable terms. The full $2,400 remains the Card Member's liability.
report.detailed_reasoning:
The allegation is RET because the Card Member says the sofa was returned or refused without a refund. CHG-A01 is the charge challenged by DSP-2026-91001: it is a posted USD 2,400 purchase charged to CRD-A01 ending 1004 and linked directly to ORD-A01. ORD-A01 is a USD 2,400 order at Hearth & Grain Furniture for one Alder three-seat sofa in Customer's Own Material. LIN-A01 and PRD-ALDER confirm that COM is the selected custom option. The transaction identity and amount are therefore established.

The order accepted POL-HGF-CO-V4 by checkbox at checkout before payment. EVI-A01-1 records that the checkbox for Checkout Terms v4 was ticked on 2026-07-02 at 14:03 before payment. Under Amex Merchant Regulations clauses 4.1 and 4.2, the retained acceptance record establishes disclosure of the accepted version. Clause CLS-HGF-CO-V4-4.3 states: "Any piece made in Customer's Own Material (COM) or made to measure is final sale and cannot be returned or refunded." The general 30-day rule in clause 4.1 applies to standard items. The Returns Page says most items can be returned within 30 days, but its exception expressly states: "Custom orders are final sale; see Checkout Terms §4.3." Thus the general language does not grant this COM order a refund right.

RTN-A01 is linked to ORD-A01 and records customer freight, refused status, and that delivery of the return was refused by the Merchant and the sofa was sent back. No refund or credit is linked to CHG-A01. The Merchant Submission and COM-A01-1 consistently identify the order as COM and final sale. Under Amex Merchant Regulations clause 4.4, the Merchant-favouring result is permitted because the specific COM exclusion is clear, unambiguous, accepted, and cross-referenced by the Returns Page. Clause 4.3 does not require a credit where the disclosed policy provides no refund entitlement.

The exact ship, arrival, and refusal dates and member-side return communications are absent. Those gaps do not change the result because even a return within 30 days would not create a refund right for a COM item absent evidence of a Merchant waiver, contrary promise, acceptance of the returned sofa, or a factual basis to disprove the COM classification. No such evidence is present.

Financial reconciliation: disputed charge USD 2,400.00, applicable refund or credit USD 0.00, other-means payment USD 0.00, resulting unreimbursed disputed amount USD 2,400.00. CHG-A02R is a separate USD 2,400 credit for CHG-A02 on a different card, Card Member, order, product option, return, and refund path; it cannot reduce this dispute.

ORD-A01 was a COM/custom sofa order. Checkout Terms v4 clause 4.3 made COM items final sale and non-refundable; the website's 30-day rule expressly excluded custom orders. RTN-A01 records a refused return, and no refund or credit was issued. The absence of exact return dates does not affect the result because the COM exclusion is not time-limited.

report.headline: $300 overcharge caused by unauthorized post-booking re-rating
report.executive_summary: The Card Member disputed $300 of a $1,300 Harbor Point Hotel charge. The connected booking, ORD-B01, was confirmed at $1,000 for two nights under Platinum Stays and guaranteed with Platinum Card CRD-B01 ending 2002. Harbor Point later settled the stay with Gold Card CRD-B02 ending 2031 and re-rated it to $1,300. That re-rating conflicts with the accepted reservation terms and applicable Amex Platinum Stays and Merchant Regulations clauses. The full $300 disputed amount is accepted for credit.
report.detailed_reasoning:
The transaction is correctly identified as CHG-B01, which is linked to ORD-B01 and Harbor Point Hotel. ORD-B01 was booked for two nights at $500 per night, for a confirmed total of $1,000, under Platinum Stays. The booking was guaranteed with the eligible Platinum Card ending 2002. The $1,300 posted charge was made to the same Card Member's Gold Card ending 2031. The Merchant's folio states that it re-rated the stay to $650 per night because settlement used the Gold Card; two nights at $650 equals the posted $1,300. This explains the arithmetic but does not establish that $1,300 was the agreed price.

The accepted Harbor Point Reservation Terms v2 state that the rate shown on the booking confirmation is the rate charged for the stay. Harbor Point's separately published Folio Terms v1, Clause 7, purport to permit re-rating when settlement uses a non-Platinum Card, but there is no record that the Card Member accepted those folio terms. In addition, the Platinum Stays participation clauses make eligibility depend on the Card used to make or guarantee the reservation, prohibit added eligibility conditions in reservation or folio terms, and require the confirmed rate to be honored. The Merchant Regulations direct that ambiguous or program-conflicting terms be read against the Merchant. Accordingly, the Gold Card settlement explains the Merchant's calculation but does not authorize changing the confirmed $1,000 rate.

The $300 difference is therefore an OVR overcharge. No linked refund, credit, Offer, tax or fee record changes the calculation. The absence of a detailed invoice does not create a defense because the booking total, posted charge, folio re-rating statement, accepted terms, and connected charge-to-order path establish the material facts needed to decide the disputed amount.

charges.rationale: The confirmed price for ORD-B01 was $1,000, while CHG-B01 posted at $1,300. The Merchant's $650-per-night re-rating was triggered solely by settlement with the Gold Card, but that post-booking condition was not accepted and conflicts with the confirmed-rate and Platinum Stays terms. The Merchant owes the full $300 difference.

report.headline: $100 Amex Offer goodwill credit approved; Northwind did not overcharge the Card Member
report.executive_summary: The disputed $100 is an Amex-funded Offer amount, not a Northwind pricing error. Northwind correctly charged the agreed $540 price for the parka and boots. The Offer was enrolled on Daniel Okafor's Platinum Card ending 3003, while the purchase posted to his separate Gold Card ending 3017, so the transaction did not qualify under the strict Card-specific Offer rule. However, the written goodwill provisions permit one Offer goodwill credit where the Offer was enrolled on another Card held by the same Card Member, the purchase otherwise met the Offer terms, and there is no earlier Offer goodwill for that Card Member. Those conditions are satisfied here. A $100 goodwill credit is therefore provided by Amex; Northwind owes no merchant-price credit.
report.detailed_reasoning:
The charge is correctly identified: DSP-2026-91003 disputes $100 of CHG-C01, a posted $540 USD purchase dated 2026-07-09. CHG-C01 was charged to active Gold Card CRD-C02 ending 3017, issued on open Gold account ACC-C02 and carried by CMB-C01. It pays ORD-C01 at Northwind Outfitters. The order total is $540, and its two line items reconcile exactly: Storm parka $390 plus trail boots $150. The merchant invoice likewise states $540 and no promo code was applied. The accepted Northwind Terms of Sale require listed-price billing and state that issuer offers are administered by the issuer, not Northwind. Accordingly, the member's expected $440 net amount was not the agreed merchant price, and the C-OVR allegation is not established against Northwind.

The $100 Offer, OFR-NWO-100, is Amex-funded, has a $500 threshold, and is valid at Northwind. It was enrolled on CRD-C01, a separate active Platinum Card ending 3003 held by the same Card Member. The $540 purchase posted to CRD-C02, not CRD-C01. CLS-AMX-OFFER-1 expressly requires payment with the specific Card on which the Offer was enrolled, even when another Card is held by the same Card Member. CLS-AMX-OFFER-3 assigns funding and statement-credit posting to Amex and states that the Merchant charges its normal price. The direct single $540 Northwind purchase satisfies the recorded merchant, direct-purchase, single-transaction, and threshold facts, apart from the enrolled-Card mismatch. No linked statement credit, refund, reversal, adjustment, or other payment exists for CHG-C01 or ORD-C01.

The strict Offer claim therefore fails against both the merchant and the normal earned-credit criteria. Nevertheless, CLS-AMX-DG-G-1 and G-2 create a separate discretionary goodwill framework. The Offer was enrolled on another Card held by CMB-C01; the purchase otherwise satisfies the recorded Offer conditions; and CMB-C01's located resolved history contains DSP-HIST-C01 with a rejected outcome, not an earlier Offer goodwill. DSP-HIST-C02's prior goodwill credit belongs to distinct Card Member CMB-C02 despite the same name and cannot disqualify this member. The appropriate disposition is goodwill_credit, with Amex funding $100 and no merchant liability.

The notebook's Northwind 'overcharge' conflict is reconciled as an expectation-versus-agreed-price issue, not a record contradiction. The Harbor Point conflict in NBK-9f39542e9 concerns a different dispute and is irrelevant to this case. The notebook's Offer-policy improvement idea is reported below because the missing validity window, exclusions, spend-calculation rules, and credit-posting timing could create or prolong similar disputes.

The $100 Offer was enrolled on CRD-C01 but the charge posted to CRD-C02, so no earned Offer credit is due under the strict Card-specific rule. Amex may nevertheless fund one Offer goodwill credit under G-1/G-2 because the Offer was on another Card of the same Card Member, the recorded purchase otherwise met the Offer conditions, and no earlier Offer goodwill exists for this Card Member. Northwind owes no price adjustment.

The dispute concerns one posted USD $5,000 purchase, CHG-D01, dated 2026-08-01 and charged to Card CRD-D01 ending 4004 at Willow Barn Venue. The applicable allegation category is PDD because the Card Member says the same wedding was paid by bank transfer and card. The evidence must therefore identify what each payment settled.

The signed Willow Barn Venue contract and INV-D01 establish a USD $6,000 venue obligation consisting of a $1,500 deposit and a $4,500 balance. PAY-D01 is a USD $1,500 bank transfer to Willow Barn Venue and settles the deposit installment. It is not a duplicate of the balance; it is the first permitted installment. CHG-D01 is linked to the balance installment, but its amount is USD $5,000 rather than the contractual USD $4,500.

PAY-D02 is a USD $4,500 bank transfer to the affiliated but distinct Willow Barn Catering merchant. Its affirmative SETTLES link is to INS-D02-FULL, the catering-in-full installment on separate invoice INV-D02. The look-alike Willow Barn names and matching amount do not override the explicit merchant, invoice, and installment links or the venue contract's clause stating that catering is separate. Accordingly, the $4,500 transfer is not established as a duplicate venue payment.

There is only one disputed card charge and no recorded second capture, reversal, refund, or credit. The full $5,000 DUP/PDD theory is therefore not supported. The merchant submission and invoice ledger say that the card paid the venue balance, but they do not explain the additional $500 or provide an itemized change order, fee, tax authorization, revised invoice, receipt, or transaction-level allocation. Under the C-OVR guide clause, the unexplained difference is an overcharge. Under Merchant Regulations clause 4.7, an amount received beyond what is due must be credited, and clause 4.3 requires that credit to go to the original Card.

The Notebook conflict entries were reviewed. They identify a factual/documentary mismatch—not a direct conflict between the accepted merchant contract and Amex policy.
